---
title: geoai-mcp-eval
short_title: Visit
description: >-
  Pre-experiment documentation for geoai-mcp-eval: does the integration interface
  (typed MCP tools vs PyQGIS code generation) change the correctness of executed
  GIS artefacts produced by an LLM agent?
---

:::{important} Pre-experiment—not frozen
![Flask](assets/icons/flask-conical.svg){width=18px} This site documents a proposed
experiment, not a finished one. The protocol is open until the preregistration tag
`v1.0-prereg`. Pages under *Findings* are explicit **ToDo** pages and are empty on
purpose. Nothing here is a result, a recommendation, or a ranking of interfaces.
:::

## The question

::::{grid} 1 1 2 2

:::{card} Main question
Does the way an LLM agent **reaches** geospatial processing operations—typed
Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools, or unrestricted code generation—change the
correctness of the artefact it actually executes?
:::

:::{card} Scope

- Nine geoprocessing operations; P/A/C task families.
- One pinned model (OpenCode-hosted BigPickle, free tier).
- One pinned engine-side oracle (ISO 19157-derived predicates; execution required).
- Confirmatory comparison: **Arm A (typed MCP) vs Arm B (PyQGIS CodeGen)**.
- N ≥ 80 tasks at scale; n = 10 pilot estimates effects only.
- Human analyst reference is **descriptive**, not an arm.
:::

::::

## Abstract (pre-experiment)

LLM agents fail on realistic tool spaces far more often than benchmarks suggest, and
half the failures are retrieval/schema errors rather than reasoning errors
[@luo2025mcpuniverse; @mo2025livemcpbench]. In geospatial work, the cost of a confident
but wrong artefact is silent corruption of the dataset, not a visibly broken demo. This
project asks whether the integration interface—typed MCP tools versus code generation—
is a *causal factor* on executed-artefact quality, holding model, engine, data and oracle
constant, and enforcing nothing about "MCP is better" in advance. The gap, the hypotheses,
the setup, and—later—the results are organised below as a single road from question to
summary.

:::{important} Pre-experiment—not frozen
This is a condensed, corpus-keyed pre-experiment review for onboarding. Every claim is
keyed to the corpus in `bibliography.bib`; nothing is imported from outside it and
nothing is invented. It orients the reader to the design; it is not the thesis's
literature review.

## How to read this page

The review answers three questions in order: **what exists** (eight evidence groups,
A–H), **why the target cell is empty** (the gap, with the adversarial floor), and
**what the evidence forces** (four design consequences, enforced in
[Experiment](../study/experiment.md)). Citations are corpus keys, rendered as bracketed
at-references; the corpus and its provenance are described in the last dropdown.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Groups A–H<br/>the evidence] --> B{Where does<br/>the cell sit?}
  B --> C[Gap: empty cell<br/>no executed-artefact interface comparison]
  C --> D[Consequences 1–4]
  D --> E[Research questions]
  E --> F[Experiment setup]
  style C fill:#fef3c7,stroke:#d97706,color:#92400e
  style A fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#1e3a8a
  style F fill:#d1fae5,stroke:#059669,color:#065f46
```

## State of the field in seven numbers

::::{grid} 1 2 4 4

:::{card} 29–44 %
frontier success on realistic MCP tool spaces; integration **degrades** with more servers [@luo2025mcpuniverse; @song2025helpor]
:::

:::{card} ≈ ½
of all failures are retrieval errors, not reasoning errors [@mo2025livemcpbench]
:::

:::{card} &lt; 25 %
GPT-4o pass^8 on τ-bench retail—single-trial success flatters reliability 20–40 pp [@yao2024taubench; @gupta2026reliabilitybench]
:::

:::{card} ≈ 32.7 %
best executed-artefact GIS agent, tolerance-strict [@gisagentbench2026]
:::

:::{card} + 26.6 pp
spatial correctness from contract + repair in code generation [@geocontra2026]
:::

:::{card} 97.14 / 85.71 %
codegen vs function calling—GeoJSON domain only, no spatial oracle [@luo2026geojson]
:::

:::{card} &lt; 57 %
end-to-end success of generated MCP projects [@yang2026mcpgen]
:::

:::{card} 42 → 95 %
agent success after grader audit in eval-discipline work—score the outcome, not the trajectory [@anthropic2026evals]
:::

::::

## The evidence, group by group

Each group below states what it covers, what it establishes, and what it leaves open.
Expand the dropdowns; nothing here substitutes for reading the primary sources.

:::{dropdown} A—GIS canon & standards (the oracle vocabulary)
**Covers.** Data-quality elements (ISO 19157; 2013 standard superseded by 19157-1:2023, element names remain the mapping vocabulary) [@iso19157]; geometry schema and topology [@iso19107]; metadata [@iso19115]; DE-9IM topological predicates [@egenhofer1991]; uncertainty of spatial data [@zhangGoodchild2002; @goodchildGopal1989; @burrough2015; @longley2015]; error propagation [@heuvelink1998]; semantics [@kuhn2005; @kuhn2012]; MAUP [@openshaw1984maup]; Jenks classification [@jenks1971]; cartography canon [@slocum2009; @maceachren1992; @monmonier2018; @harrowerBrewer2003]; ISO-style quality framing for LLM outputs [@shingleton2025geoquality].

**Establishes.** The oracle's predicate families are standard GIScience quality elements—not bespoke checks, not vibes.

**Leaves open.** Which predicates bind to which interfaces, and whether enforcement depth at the tool boundary changes what ships. That is the experiment, not the canon.
:::

:::{dropdown} B—Autonomous GIS (what agents demonstrably do)
**Covers.** Vision and autonomy levels [@li2023autonomous; @li2025autonomous]; retrieval agents [@ning2025autonomous]; QGIS-as-tools multi-agent systems, fine-tuning for execution success (100 % exec / 87.5 % semantic; ceiling degrades with complexity) [@mansourian2026multiagent]; code-generation multi-agents with RAG over syntax corpora (+7.59–26.09 % gains) [@wu2025geocolab]; MCTS over programs [@chen2024geoagent]; 1 800 controlled end-to-end runs with Cliff's δ and Kendall τ = 0.94—single-agent ReAct beats dual-agent orchestration on cloud backends [@han2026gisclaw]; 1 778 expert reasoning steps with step-wise scoring [@shabbir2025thinkgeo]; open-weight cost–capability (≈ 93 % of Claude's capability at 11.6× lower cost) [@diazireland2026geonatureagent]; maturity snapshots [@liang2026geoagentic; @openearthagent2026].

**Establishes.** GIS agents exist across the autonomy spectrum, and the bottleneck is executional reliability—not intent, not planning prose.

**Leaves open.** Whether the interface (typed MCP vs code generation)—rather than the model, the harness, or the prompt—moves executed-artefact correctness.
:::

:::{dropdown} C—Protocols (what MCP is and how fragile it is)
**Covers.** The normative specification [@anthropicMCP]; ecosystem reviews [@nargund2025mcp; @strickland2026pareto; @mastouri2025automcp]—88.6 % of servers are REST wrappers, a median 19 % of operations exposed, catalogues are edited artefacts, generated servers go 76 % → 94.2 % after repair; catalogue sizing as a controlled variable, 4-tool optimum, +16.4 pp completion vs fine-grained primitives [@paschalides2026mcpgranite]; a 16-lifecycle-activity threat taxonomy across 16 scenarios and four attacker classes [@hou2025mcp]; protocol-level flaws with ATTEST-style repair (MCP amplifies attack success by 23–41 %) [@maloyan2026breaking]; 12 attacks / 2 000 instances with an NRP robustness metric—stronger models are *more* vulnerable [@zhang2025msb]; error accumulation O(√T) with re-grounding ≈ every 9 steps [@fan2026infofidelity]; OGC lineage (WPS 2.0 / OGC API Processes) [@ogcWps2; @ogcApiProcesses]; adjacent client protocol [@agentClientProtocol].

**Establishes.** The protocol is real, fragile, and catalogue-sensitive; enforcement at the boundary is a live design axis, not a detail.

**Leaves open.** Whether enforcement depth is *the* mechanism, separable from protocol identity—the C3 claim of this study.
:::

:::{dropdown} D—General tool-use & agent benchmarks (instrument canon + grim baseline)
**Covers.** pass^k methodology [@yao2024taubench]; ReliabilityBench's R(k,ε,λ) surface [@gupta2026reliabilitybench]; MCP-Atlas (claim-coverage@0.75; 63.3 % cognitive failures) [@bandi2026mcpatlas]; MCP-Bench (28 servers, 250 tools, cross-tool coupling) [@wang2025mcpbench]; LiveMCP-101 (7 failure modes; TSR/ARS) [@yin2025livemcp]; MCPToolBench++ (AST score, 4 k servers) [@fan2025mcptoolbench]; LiveMCPBench (retrieval ≈ ½ of failures) [@mo2025livemcpbench]; MCP-Universe (frontier 29–44 %; dilution) [@luo2025mcpuniverse]; MCPGAUGE (integration degrades effectiveness) [@song2025helpor]; GeoMCP's publish–find–bind design (a design precedent, not effectiveness evidence) [@ogsagent2026]; eval discipline—grade the outcome, not the trajectory (CORE-Bench 42 → 95 % after grader audit) [@anthropic2026evals].

**2026 wave.** Executed-project generation [@yang2026mcpgen]; live-server effect scoring with pass^3 collapse [@kaminski2026dynamicmcpbench]; evolution robustness across 123 servers [@liu2026mcpevolbench].

**Establishes.** The measurement machinery (pass^k, claim coverage, live servers) and the grim baseline—every instrument this experiment borrows already exists.

**Leaves open.** All of it in the GIS regime, under an ISO-predicate oracle, on the interface axis.
:::

:::{dropdown} E—GIS-agent benchmarks (the competitive set)
**Covers.** GeoAnalystBench (50 expert tasks; code-style validity ≠ correctness—"right shape, wrong numbers") [@zhang2025geoanalystbench]; GeoAgentBench (PEA metric, Last-Attempt Alignment; Plan-and-React > ReAct; ≈117–133 tools—cite the published version) [@yu2026geoagentbench]; GISAgentBench (349 tasks, strict tolerances, 32.7 % best-case, IoU ≥ 0.5) [@gisagentbench2026]; GeoBenchX (unsolvable-task rejection scoring) [@krechetova2025geobenchx]; GeoContra (contracts + repair, +26.6 pp, 7 079 tasks / 11 models) [@geocontra2026]; ThinkGeo, OpenEarthAgent, GeoNatureAgent [@shabbir2025thinkgeo; @openearthagent2026; @diazireland2026geonatureagent].

**Establishes.** Executed GIS benchmarks exist, are brutal, and measure the wrong factor—none manipulates the interface with an ISO predicate oracle.

**Leaves open.** Exactly the cell in the next section.
:::

:::{dropdown} F—MCP × GIS (the thin intersection everyone claims and nobody operationalised)
**Covers.** The GeoJSON head-to-head (codegen 97.14 % vs function calling 85.71 %) [@luo2026geojson]; tool-exposure guidance for GNSS toolchains [@tool_exposure_gnss_2026]; GeoMCP server design [@ogsagent2026]; discovery-MCP benchmark (agents on par with humans on parts of metadata search) [@ichms2026_mcp_geodata]; the ICHMS GIS-MCP cluster [@gis-mcp-server-cluster-2026].

**Establishes.** What exists: systems, specs, and one non-GIS, non-oracle-scored head-to-head. What does not exist: an executed-artefact comparison on the interface axis with ISO predicates.

**Leaves open.** The entire question—this experiment is that comparison.
:::

:::{dropdown} G—Cartographic judgement (the C-family counter-case)
**Covers.** ColourBrewer compliance [@harrowerBrewer2003]; intent-driven colour [@gauslaa2026intentcolour]; choropleth LLM case [@pannoon2025choropleth]; visual variables [@maceachren1992; @slocum2009]; map-abuse canon [@monmonier2018]; Jenks classification [@jenks1971].

**Establishes.** Cartography is judgeable but not oracle-gradable pass/fail; it is consumed here as *descriptors* (pre-registered counter-case), never as a gate.

**Leaves open.** Whether cartographic tasks behave differently under the two interfaces—pre-registered as the RQ3 counter-case.
:::

:::{dropdown} H—Method (why the design looks like this)
**Covers.** Design-science research [@peffers2007design]; the analysis kit—paired binary tests, mixed models, gatekeeping, minimum detectable effects [@anthropic2026evals]; agent-run reproducibility practice [@nust2018; @konkol2019]; instrument/usability framing [@nivala2008]; pass^k as the reliability unit (Group D/E).

**Establishes.** The method is standard; the novelty is the enforced constant on every axis except the interface.

**Leaves open.** Nothing methodological—everything depends on freeze discipline (see [Hypotheses](../study/hypotheses.md)).
:::

## The gap—the empty cell

:::{important} The empty cell (verbatim logic)
No study holds **engine + model + data + oracle constant**, manipulates **only the integration interface** (typed MCP vs code generation), and scores **executed GIS artefacts** against ISO 19157 predicates under **repetition (pass^k)**, with contamination-aware strata and preregistered tolerances.
:::

Why the cell is still empty, in five independent reasons [@mastouri2025automcp; @iso19157]:

| # | Why it survives |
|---|---|
| 1 | It is expensive—N runs × N tasks × N interfaces, and GIS artefacts need per-tool predicates |
| 2 | The answer is telegraphed directionally (GeoJSON 97 / 86; MCPGAUGE degradation) [@luo2026geojson; @song2025helpor] |
| 3 | Scoring asymmetry—code artefacts execute freely; tool artefacts need per-tool checks |
| 4 | Catalogue confounds make "MCP" ill-defined as a treatment [@mastouri2025automcp] |
| 5 | GIS semantics (CRS, topology, MAUP) punish weak judges [@iso19157; @openshaw1984maup; @egenhofer1991] |

**Nearest neighbours and what they leave open**—ten works, each filling part of the cell, none the whole:

| Work | What it fixes | What remains open |
|---|---|---|
| GeoJSON Agents [@luo2026geojson] | head-to-head interface comparison | different domain, FC≠MCP protocol, multi-agent confound, non-spatial judging |
| GeoContra [@geocontra2026] | contracts + repair for codegen | no MCP arm; task templates, not the interface factor |
| GeoAgentBench [@yu2026geoagentbench] | executed sandbox + PEA | tool-calling only; no codegen arm; non-typed catalogue |
| GISAgentBench [@gisagentbench2026] | artefact ground truth; tolerances | no interface manipulation; binary match, not ISO predicates |
| MCPGen [@yang2026mcpgen] | executed MCP projects, <57 % e2e | project generation, not the interface factor, not GIS |
| DynamicMCPBench [@kaminski2026dynamicmcpbench] | live-server effect scoring | general domains; single-configuration |
| MCPEvol-Bench [@liu2026mcpevolbench] | 123-server evolution robustness | different question (drift); enables the frozen-catalogue rule |
| ReliabilityBench [@gupta2026reliabilitybench] | pass^k methodology | scheduling/travel domain; no interface factor |
| Shingleton & Basiri [@shingleton2025geoquality] | ISO-style quality for LLM outputs | geoparsing scale only; not multi-tool artefacts |
| Discovery MCP [@ichms2026_mcp_geodata] | MCP discovery vs humans | metadata search, not artefact execution |

:::{warning} Adversarial floor (what would close the gap)
Any 2026–2027 work doing GIS artefact MCP-vs-codegen with executed ISO scoring appearing
before freeze forces this study to re-scope to the mechanism leg (enforcement depth,
C3) and the instrument (C1). The headline falls; the science survives—the
re-scoping rule is written now, not negotiated later.
:::

**Synthesis in one line.** The field is code-generation-first for GIS [@li2023autonomous; @li2025autonomous; @wu2025geocolab] and MCP-first only as design [@ogsagent2026]; every benchmark manipulates models or architectures, none manipulates the **interface paradigm** with executed, ISO-scored artefacts—and the 2026 wave sharpened execution difficulty and liveness, not the factor.

## What the evidence forces (design consequences)

::::{grid} 1 1 2 2

:::{card} 1—The interface is the only difference
Catalogue constant: one server, one tool surface, one hash; depth is a single flag. Anything else measures catalogue design, not the interface [@mastouri2025automcp; @paschalides2026mcpgranite].
:::

:::{card} 2—The oracle is the judge
Correctness is defined by executed-artefact predicates (ISO 19157 family), never by LLM judgement or human impression [@iso19157; @anthropic2026evals; @shingleton2025geoquality].
:::

:::{card} 3—Leakage is a stratum, not a hope
Inherited vs constructed tasks are analysed separately; inherited tasks demand CC BY-SA attribution and contamination tags (see [Provenance](../provenance.md)).
:::

:::{card} 4—Reliability is pass^k
One success is not success; r = 4 repetitions per task, reported as pass^4 with ICC—the unit of evidence is repeatability [@yao2024taubench; @gupta2026reliabilitybench].
:::

::::

These four consequences bind the [research questions](research-questions.md), the [hypotheses](../study/hypotheses.md), and the [experiment setup](../study/experiment.md).

:::{dropdown} Corpus administration (how to trust the citations)
The corpus is 81 entries in `bibliography.bib`, plain biblatex, each carrying fulltext open-access provenance (record source, retrieval date, licence). No paywall-sourced full text; every key cited on this page resolves in the corpus snapshot shipped with this site; keys are never invented. Groups A–H organise the evidence in the order the design was assembled. If a claim matters, the key sits next to it—if a key is missing, the claim does not ship.
:::

# === review/research-questions.md ===

---
title: Research questions
short_title: RQs
description: >-
  The research questions raised by the gap, with pre-registered hypotheses and
  nulls verbatim from the frozen post-consultation specification (§6.1).
---

(research-questions)=

:::{warning} Pre-experiment—not frozen
Nulls are quoted from the frozen specification (post-professor-consultation,
two-sided, paired). They become append-only at freeze (`v1.0-prereg`); before that,
they are design, not evidence.
:::

Hierarchical gatekeeping—RQ1, RQ2 gate; RQ8 follows; everything else is secondary
or descriptive. **At n = 10 (pilot) nothing is confirmatory; the pilot estimates
effects and validates the instrument. Confirmatory claims live in the scaled study
(N ≥ 80).**

## Confirmatory family (gate order)

::::{grid} 1 1 2 2

:::{card} RQ1—interface factor (gate)
Does the interface change executed-artefact success rate on geoprocessing tasks?

**H₀:** π_MCP = π_CG (two-sided, direction unspecified).

Paired exact McNemar on discordant tasks; bootstrap 95 % CI on ΔWSZ; Cliff's δ.
:::

:::{card} RQ2—enforcement-depth curve (gate)
Does WSZ rise with enforcement depth at the boundary (N1→N4)?

**H₀:** β_linear = 0 (linear contrast); secondary plateau **H₀:** WSZ(N4) − WSZ(N3) = 0.

Ordinal contrast on per-run WSZ; plateau contrast. Mechanism leg; only if the N-flag
is implemented (see [Experiment](../study/experiment.md)).
:::

:::{card} RQ8—silent corruption
Does enforcement ≥ N2 eliminate executable-but-invalid artefacts that codegen ships
silently?

**H₀:** silent-invalid rate (CG or N≤1) = silent-invalid rate (≥ N2).

Exact Fisher; odds ratio + CI. The GIS-specific causal claim; predicates double as
boundary checks, so the (enforced ∩ oracle) enumeration is mandatory pre-freeze.
:::

:::{card} RQ3—expressible-share moderation
Does the interface delta grow with task expressibility (P/A/C; low/med/high)?

**H₀:** paradigm × expressible-share interaction = 0.

Exploratory at 10 tasks; confirmatory only at scale. Cartography is the pre-registered
counter-case.
:::

::::

## Secondary family (Hochberg within family)

::::{grid} 1 1 2 2

:::{card} RQ6—reliability
Do arms differ in pass^4 / ICC?

**H₀:** pass⁴_MCP = pass⁴_CG. Small-sample exact; ICC by arm.
:::

:::{card} RQ4—failure taxonomy
Do arms distribute failures differently (interface-adjacent vs workflow-silent vs
hallucinated structure)?

**H₀:** multinomial distributions identical. Exact multinomial; double-coded
subsample, Cohen's κ ≥ 0.6.
:::

::::

## Descriptive family (estimates + CIs only; never p-vibes)

| ID | Question |
|---|---|
| RQ5 | Cost per *successful* task (requests, tool-calls, wall-clock; $ only with a stable price table) |
| RQ-E | Deployed-pattern arm (MCP + `execute_code`): bypass/collapse rate; ΔWSZ vs pure MCP |
| RQ-C | Code-as-driver arm (Python → typed MCP tools): ΔWSZ vs A and vs B; trajectory classification |
| RQ-PH | Human reference (GUI-first): WSZ_h, human_time_min, human_steps; same oracle; descriptive |
| RQ-I | Instrument integrity: 3× oracle determinism; log completeness; 0 silently dropped runs |

**Out of scope (pre-declared):** model × paradigm interaction; security frontier; VGI
moderator; human verification cost; live-vs-mock servers (the reference server is
deterministic and logged—declared assumption).

See [Hypotheses](../study/hypotheses.md) for the inferential contract that binds these RQs
together, and [Experiment](../study/experiment.md) for the arms that answer them.

# === study/hypotheses.md ===

---
title: Hypotheses & inferential contract
short_title: Hypotheses
description: >-
  Nulls, decision rules, multiple-comparison discipline, and what counts as evidence—
  the contract that binds the research questions at freeze.
---

(hypotheses)=

:::{warning} Pre-experiment—not frozen
Append-only from freeze. Changing anything here after `v1.0-prereg` invalidates the
run log.
:::

## Two regimes of evidence

| Regime | n | What it yields | Claim status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pilot (3 tasks × {A@N3, B} × r=2) | 12 runs + replications | Instrument validation; effect-size estimates | Never confirmatory |
| Pilot suite (10 tasks × 5 configs × r=4) | 200 runs (+160 stretch) | Estimates, CIs, instrument audits | Estimates only |
| Scaled study | N ≥ 80 tasks × r=4 | Tests of the confirmatory family | Confirmatory |

## Hypotheses and nulls (by gate order)

| Gate | Hypothesis | Null (verbatim) | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | RQ1 interface factor | π_MCP = π_CG (two-sided) | Exact McNemar on discordant pairs; bootstrap 95 % CI on ΔWSZ (10 000 task resamples); Cliff's δ |
| 2 | RQ2 enforcement-depth curve | β_linear = 0 (linear contrast); plateau: WSZ(N4) − WSZ(N3) = 0 | Ordinal contrast; plateau contrast |
| 3 | RQ8 silent corruption | silent-invalid rate (CG or N≤1) = silent-invalid rate (≥ N2) | Exact Fisher; odds ratio + CI |
|—| RQ3 moderation (exploratory at pilot) | paradigm × expressible-share interaction = 0 | Stratified ΔWSZ with CIs |
| 4 | RQ6 reliability (secondary) | pass⁴_MCP = pass⁴_CG | Small-sample exact; ICC by arm |
| 4 | RQ4 failure taxonomy (secondary) | multinomial distributions identical | Exact multinomial; double-coded κ ≥ 0.6 gate |

## Discipline

- **Two-sided, paired.** Discordant tasks are the data; ties are uninformative.
- **Hierarchical gatekeeping** in the order RQ1 → RQ2 → RQ8 → (RQ6, RQ4). Failure at a
  gate stops the inference chain. Familywise α = .05; no peeks.
- **Hochberg** within the secondary family.
- **Descriptive** families (RQ5, RQ-E, RQ-C, RQ-PH, RQ-I) report estimates and CIs
  only—never p-values, never rankings ("MCP better/worse" is out of bounds at this stage).
- **Silent corruption** is the one latent GIS failure mode the design privileges:
  executable-but-invalid artefacts that pass casual inspection. Predicates double as
  boundary checks; the (enforced ∩ oracle) enumeration is mandatory pre-freeze.
- **No** mixed-effects models, power claims, or MDE claims at n = 10; underpowered
  tests are reported as uninformative, not as nulls.
- **Scale path**: at N ≥ 80, descriptive tags swap to confirmatory—same machinery,
  powered—with strata analyses retained and (if runs span weeks) a sequential-monitoring audit.

## What would count as evidence

At freeze, a claim of the form "the interface changes executed-artefact success" is
licensed only if RQ1 clears its gate with a two-sided exact McNemar on discordant
tasks, a bootstrap 95 % CI on ΔWSZ excluding (or including, direction-free) zero, and
the oracle-determinism + completeness gates (3× identical verdicts; 200/200 or N≥80×4
runs logged, no silent imputation). Anything weaker is reported as an estimate.

See [Experiment](experiment.md) for the design that produces those numbers, and
[Results](../findings/results.md) for where they will appear.

# === study/experiment.md ===

---
title: Experiment setup
short_title: Experiment
description: >-
  Arms A/B/C/D/H, catalogue-constant rule, task-suite v1 proposal, freeze order,
  and scoring—the operational design behind the research questions.
---

(experiment)=

:::{warning} Pre-experiment—not frozen
The protocol is open until freeze. Everything on this page is a rendering of the frozen
specification (post-consultation); the specification wins on any disagreement. Arms C, D
are exploratory descriptors, not inferential factors.
:::

## Arms and factors

| Arm | Configuration | Role in inference |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | Typed MCP only; N-flag middleware (primary execution at N3; full N-curve only if budget permits) | **Confirmatory (vs B)** |
| **B** | CodeGen: Python free execution (PyQGIS/GeoPandas/…); post-hoc oracle checks only (N0) | **Confirmatory (vs A)** |
| **C** | Typed MCP + one `execute_code` tool (mirrors deployed QGIS-MCP plugins) | Exploratory descriptor—bounds realism; may collapse to B by construction |
| **D** | Agent generates Python that calls the typed MCP tools (client inside script) | Exploratory descriptor—practitioner pattern; N-flag still gates every call |
| **H** | Human analysts, GUI-first | Reference, not inference |

**Factors.** Paradigm (A vs B; C, D exploratory) · enforcement depth N1–N4 within arm A
(middleware flag; catalogue constant) · task family P/A/C (blocking) · expressible share
(moderator) · contamination stratum (inherited/constructed) · repetition r = 4.

:::{important} Catalogue-constant rule (non-negotiable)
One server, one tool surface, one catalogue hash; depth is a single flag
(`--enforce=N1..N4`). If this cannot be held constant, the experiment measures
catalogue design, not the interface.
:::

## Task suite (v1, to freeze after pilot)

- **Proposed initial suite:** 10 tasks—4 P (prepare/IO), 4 A (analysis), 2 C (cartography);
  contamination ≈ 50/50 inherited/constructed; difficulty tiers 1–4.
- **Mandatory traps:** at least one raster task, one topology/DE-9IM task, one
  CRS/axis-order trap, one Jenks/classification task, one zonation/aggregation trap
  (MAUP), one NoData trap [@openshaw1984maup; @iso19157].
- **YAML schema v1** (frozen at freeze): stable `id`, P/A/C family, difficulty rubric
  (n_tools_human, n_steps_human), provenance (source, licence, contamination tag),
  human baseline produced before agent runs, oracle (≥3 determinism runs, tiered
  assertions), budget bounds. Validation: schema check, unique ids, every oracle type
  implemented, licence strings present—all CI-enforced pre-freeze.
- **Licensing:** inherited GIS StackExchange tasks are CC BY-SA 4.0 (attribution mandatory);
  author-constructed tasks are CC0—see [Provenance](../provenance.md).

## Demand anchor (GIS Stack Exchange; supplied counts, retrieval date unverified)

The full analysis (method, all 29 counts, 27-row complexity ranking, catalogue gaps) is on the [SE demand analysis](../analysis.md) page; the anchor table:

| Operation | SE tag count | Operation | SE tag count |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| buffer | 1 533 | spatial join | 1 014 |
| clip | 1 391 | zonal statistics | 572 |
| merge | 1 284 | dissolve | 547 |
| raster calculator | 1 296 | overlay | 512 |
| field calculator | 2 562 | jenks | 9 |

Jenks at 9 is a counter-case by design—it tests the pre-registered cartography
hypothesis on the literature, not on SE volume. Counts measure demand, not difficulty
[@mastouri2025automcp]; they select tasks, they validate nothing—the oracle decides
correctness. Known catalogue gaps to close before freeze (legitimate instrument changes):
field calculator; merge; ideally point_distance.

## Freeze order

1. **Pilot**—3 tasks × {A@N3, B} × r=2; verify the whole chain (fixture → dispatch →
   artefact → oracle → log); tune task bugs only, never oracle thresholds post-hoc.
2. **Pre-freeze audit**—directory hash, fixture checksums, task-suite validator,
   oracle 3× determinism, human baseline H executed + oracle-verified, contamination
   spot-audit.
3. **Freeze**—tag `v1.0-prereg` (specification + task checksums + seed table).
4. **Runs**—stratum-interleaved randomisation; fresh session per run; the run directory archived automatically.
5. **Completeness assertion**—N≥80×4 runs logged; any missing run breaks the analysis
   family, documented, never silently imputed.

## Scoring and analysis (by reference)

Scored on executed artefacts via ISO 19157-derived predicates (tiers A–D: existence →
spatial predicates → value-level vs baseline → repeatability/economics). The formal
scoring contract (WSZ/OQS definitions, weights, tie handling) and the full analysis plan
with its limits are defined in the specification §§6.7–6.8 and are intentionally **not**
restated here. Preregistration → **Załącznik E** (outside this repository).

## Threats and the human reference

Top threats (model pinning, provider drift, ceiling effects, catalogue confounds,
oracle bugs, prompt sensitivity, leakage, judging validity) and the human-reference
protocol (same oracle, screen-capture, processing.log parsing, report appended only
after agent-run analysis is locked) are specified in the frozen specification §§6.6,
6.9, 6.10. The human analyst is a **descriptive reference, not a baseline to beat**.

# === study/implementation.md ===

---
title: Implementation status
short_title: Implementation
description: >-
  Current implementation and the engineering constraints carried into the run
  (pins, logging, deviations); study results remain unfrozen.
---

(implementation)=

:::{warning} Pre-experiment—not frozen
The repository includes an experiment CLI scaffold and a QGIS plugin prototype. The
study protocol and results remain unfrozen; this page distinguishes implemented
scaffolding from planned or unverified study behavior.
:::

## Implementation snapshot (state supplied; date not independently verified)

| Layer | State |
|---|---|
| Repository scaffold (pixi, Tasknest, alint, rumdl, Vale, CI, Pages) | Present; MyST docs added (this site) |
| Experiment code (`experiment/`) | Typer CLI and smoke tests; pilot task suite not frozen |
| Task suite | Not frozen; YAML schema v1 designed, tasks not written |
| MCP server / catalogue | Not built; catalogue constant hash pending |
| Oracle / checkers library | Not built; determinism gate untested |
| Model access | OpenCode-hosted BigPickle (free tier; daily request limit; no durable pinning, seed or token accounting) |
| Human baseline | Not run |

## Engineering constraints (carried into the run)

- **Model:** log `model_id`, `run_date`, driver hash, temperature on every record;
  provider drift is unmeasured variance bounded by r = 4; results are never reported as
  "BigPickle shows…" beyond this scope.
- **Runtime:** Python 3; `mcp` client; `geopandas`, `shapely`, `pyproj`, `rasterio`,
  `pyogrio`; QGIS LTR via a dedicated profile; PROJ/GDAL versions pinned and recorded.
- **Environment:** `pixi install --locked`; the `experiment` feature is currently
  included in the default environment with tooling. The docs environment has its own
  solve group. Split the GIS stack before measurement runs if it affects tooling
  reproducibility. Nothing runs Python via `uv`/`pip`/`venv` inside this repo.
- **Determinism:** oracle 3× identical verdicts on fixed artefacts is a blocking gate.
- **Logging:** independent fresh session per run; wall-clock timestamps; the run directory `results/<run_id>/` archived automatically; 0 silently dropped runs; logged artefacts are never edited
  post-hoc.
- **Measurement limits:** token accounting may be missing (no stable price table assumed);
  proxies only, never fabricated zeros.

## Deviations log

No deviations are recorded yet—nothing has been run. When the study executes, every
deviation from the registered protocol will be documented here, with its rationale and
its blast radius. Silence means fidelity, not absence of drift to look for.

## What appears at freeze

The frozen catalogue hash and validator results, the checkers' coverage of every oracle
type in the suite, the pilot report (instrument health, wall-clock, failure heuristics),
and the `v1.0-prereg` preregistration tag (specification + task checksums + seed table)
will appear here as recorded facts, not plans. Until then this page is a statement of
intent—see [Reproducibility](../reproducibility.md) for the contract.

(results)=

:::{warning} ToDo—nothing has been run yet
![ToDo](../assets/icons/triangle-alert.svg){width=18px} The protocol is not yet in
execution. There are no results, figures or tables to report. This page is a
reserved, empty slot in the arc—it will be filled after the freeze and the
completeness check.
:::

## What this page will contain

- **RQ1 (gate):** exact McNemar on discordant task pairs; bootstrap 95 % CI on ΔWSZ
  (10 000 resamples); Cliff's δ—estimates only until N ≥ 80.
- **RQ2:** enforcement-depth contrast (if the N-curve ran); plateau contrast N3→N4.
- **RQ8:** silent-invalid rates by arm; odds ratio + CI.
- **RQ6 / RQ4:** pass^4, ICC by arm; failure taxonomy with the κ ≥ 0.6 double-coding gate.
- **RQ5 / RQ-E / RQ-C / RQ-PH / RQ-I:** descriptive estimates + CIs.
- **Instrument audits:** oracle 3× determinism; completeness check (no missing runs).

Every number will carry its CI; P/A/C and inherited/constructed strata will be reported
separately; figures will be static committed images generated from the frozen pipeline.

# === findings/interpretation.md ===

---
title: Interpretation (ToDo)
short_title: Interpretation
description: >-
  ToDo—interpretation of the results against the frozen hypotheses, written after
  the analysis is locked and the human-reference report is appended.
---

(interpretation)=

:::{warning} ToDo—not started
![ToDo](../assets/icons/triangle-alert.svg){width=18px} Interpretation happens after
the agent-run analysis is locked and the human-reference report is appended (the human
report is appended after, not before, the analysis is locked). Nothing here is a
finding.
:::

## What this page will contain

- Gate-order verdicts (RQ1 → RQ2 → RQ8 → RQ3/RQ6/RQ4); failure at a gate truncates
  the chain.
- Mechanism reading: contract-enforcement depth vs protocol identity—the transferable
  claim, not a "MCP wins/loses" headline.
- Where the interface delta lives (P/A/C; inherited vs constructed; expressible share).
- Which failures are interface-adjacent vs workflow-silent vs hallucinated structure,
  with the double-coded κ ≥ 0.6 quality gate.
- How far enforcement ≥ N2 eliminates executable-but-invalid artefacts that code generation
  ships silently—the GIS-specific causal claim.
- What the r = 4 design and the pilot-vs-scaled distinction can and cannot bound.

Every interpretive sentence will trace to a number on [Results](results.md) or to the
frozen design. No result will be generalized beyond this model, this catalogue and this
task suite.

  and what would falsify it.

(summary)=

:::{warning} ToDo—written last
![ToDo](../assets/icons/triangle-alert.svg){width=18px} A summary written before
data is a prediction dressed as a conclusion. This page stays empty until the analysis
is locked.
:::

## What this page will contain

- A one-paragraph answer to the main question, licensed only by the RQ1 gate outcome,
  in neutral language.
- The three-leg claim, updated to whatever survived the data: **instrument** (the
  frozen harness: tasks-as-YAML, predicate oracle, results contract) · **estimate, not
  declaration** (effect size + intervals at a stated power limit) · **mechanism**
  (enforcement depth N1–N4 vs protocol identity).
- Limits: what N, seeds and provider drift permit claiming; what would falsify the
  mechanism reading.
- What the instrument enables next: the scaled study (N ≥ 80) and the re-scoping rule
  if stronger counter-evidence appears.

Claims will cite only the corpus bibliography; no new sources are introduced at summary
time.


**Result.** The top-voted questions for the six seeded candidate tags (votes desc, up to 5 pages × 25 each), projected to `tag, question_id, title, score, view_count, answer_count, license, link`; sorted by score desc. From the embedded snapshot—zero API calls. (750, 8).

```{marimo} python
    pd.DataFrame(SNAPSHOT["questions"])
    .sort_values("score", ascending=False, ignore_index=True)
)
print(questions.shape)
questions.head()
```

**Result.** Per-tag question counts for the 29 operational tags from `tags/{tags}/info`, sorted by `questions` desc. From the embedded snapshot—zero API calls. (29, 2).

## Caveats

- Votes measure visibility/confusion, not workload frequency; tiers are expert estimates.
- The supplied snapshot has no independently verified retrieval date; all-time counts drift upward slowly. The curated [SE demand analysis](../analysis.md) page carries the aggregates used for task selection.
- Not a freeze artifact; the oracle decides correctness. Every item is CC BY-SA 4.0.

:::{dropdown} Regenerating the snapshot (manual; ~31 anonymous API quota units)
The cells above never touch the network. To refresh the embedded data, run this recipe outside the site (Python with `stackapi` and `pandas`; a key is optional), then paste the printed JSON into `SNAPSHOT_JSON` and bump `SNAPSHOT_FETCHED`:

```python
import json

import pandas as pd
from stackapi import StackAPI

TAGS_INFO = ["coordinate-system","dem","distance","buffer","clip","raster-calculator","merge",
             "spatial-join","interpolation","geocoding","topology","routing","zonal-statistics",
             "dissolve","overlay","snapping","union","kriging","nodata","intersect","simplify",
             "reverse-geocoding","choropleth","network-analysis","erase","jenks","raster","shapefile","qgis"]
QUESTION_TAGS = ["buffer","clip","spatial-join","overlay","zonal-statistics","dissolve"]

site = StackAPI("gis", key=None, max_pages=5)  # anonymous quota: 300/day

tag_counts = (
    pd.DataFrame(site.fetch("tags/{tags}/info", tags=";".join(TAGS_INFO), pagesize=100)["items"])
    [["name", "count"]].rename(columns={"name": "tag", "count": "questions"})
    .sort_values("questions", ascending=False, ignore_index=True))
rows = []
for tag in QUESTION_TAGS:
    raw = site.fetch("questions", tagged=tag, order="desc", sort="votes", pagesize=25)
    rows.extend({"tag": tag, **q} for q in raw["items"])
questions = (pd.DataFrame(rows).rename(columns={"content_license": "license"})
             [["tag", "question_id", "title", "score", "view_count",
               "answer_count", "license", "link"]]
             .sort_values("score", ascending=False, ignore_index=True))

print(json.dumps({"fetched": "YYYY-MM-DD", "site": "gis",
                    "tag_counts": tag_counts.to_dict("records"),
                    "questions": questions.to_dict("records")},
                  separators=(",", ":")))
```

:::

(provenance)=

## Sources and date

| Item | Value |

## Aggregate demand (selected, all-time counts)

| Tag | Count | Tag | Count |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| raster (broad) | 10 203 | spatial-join | 1 014 |
| coordinate-system | 8 647 | geocoding | 870 |
| field-calculator | 2 562 | zonal-statistics | 572 |
| dem | 2 113 | dissolve | 547 |

The full method, frequency tables, the 27-row complexity ranking and catalogue-gap analysis live in the [SE demand analysis](analysis.md) page. Top-voted questions are roughly half **conceptual explainers** (EPSG:3857 vs 4326, datum
vs projection, axis order)—inherited tasks deliberately target exactly these confusion
points.

## Method in one paragraph

All-time counts per tag were pulled from the SE API (no time series, no geography
filter). Vote counts on the top-100 questions track conceptual confusion, not operational
need. Complexity tiers attached to tasks come from the task-suite difficulty rubric as expert
estimates, not measurements.

## Limitations

- Counts are all-time and tool-ecosystem-skewed (ArcGIS|QGIS dominate); no time series, no geography filter, English-only.
- Votes on the top-100 track **conceptual confusion**, not operational need; ~half the headline questions are CRS/datum explainers.
- Tag counts confound "asking" with "doing"; many high-count tags are installation/config/software topics, not tasks.
- Complexity tiers are expert estimates, not measurements; they anchor on the spec's rubric, pending pilot calibration.
- "Most common GIS tasks ranked by complexity" is not a number GIS.SE publishes; the analysis is a synthesis, not a dump.
- Licensing: inherited prompts must preserve attribution; constructed traps are the low-risk default.

## Licensing obligations (binding)

- Every inherited question is **CC BY-SA 4.0**. Attribution (link + licence) is recorded
  in each task's `provenance.source` / `provenance.license` fields; the complete
  attribution list will be deposited in the repository at freeze, listing every
  inherited item individually.
- Closed/locked questions may lack a license field; **do not derive from them**.
- Author-constructed tasks are **CC0-equivalent** (no attribution required); they carry
  `contamination: constructed` and remain the low-risk default where SE signal is absent.
- This site's prose is CC BY-SA 4.0; the repository code scaffold is MIT (see LICENSE).

## The load-bearing caveat

**GIS StackExchange selects tasks; it validates nothing.** Frequency measures demand,
never correctness. Artefact correctness is decided solely by the predicate oracle—see
[Experiment](study/experiment.md) and [Hypotheses](study/hypotheses.md).

# === analysis.md ===

---
title: SE demand analysis—is the task bank representative?
short_title: SE demand analysis
description: >-
  GIS Stack Exchange demand as a representability proxy for the geoprocessing task
  bank: method, frequency tables, complexity ranking, catalogue gaps, and limits.
  Supplied snapshot with an unverified retrieval date.
---

(gis-analysis)=

:::{warning} Supplied snapshot—not a live or independently verified dataset
The figures are all-time counts embedded in the supplied GIS Stack Exchange snapshot.
Its retrieval date and values have not been independently verified here; treat the
counts and derived findings as provisional until the source is re-fetched and checked.
The raw source lives in the [GIS.SE analysis (raw marimo notebook)](analyses/gis-se-analysis.md)
page and renders offline. GIS.SE **selects tasks; it validates nothing**—the oracle
decides correctness.
:::

## What this analysis is (and is not)

::::{grid} 1 1 2 2

:::{card} What it is
A representability scout for the task bank: which geoprocessing operations GIS
practitioners actually ask about, how they rank by execution complexity, and where the
proposed tool surface is blind. All counts are question-tag frequencies, English-only,
tool-ecosystem-skewed toward desktop QGIS/ArcGIS.
:::

:::{card} What it is not
Not a frequency-of-practice measure, not difficulty, not importance, not evidence
that any tool or interface works. It anchors task selection and contamination strata —
never scoring, never the oracle.
:::

::::

## Method (as described in the supplied source; not independently verified)

:::{dropdown} Full method

- **API**: public Stack Exchange API, `site=gis`, no scraping; all content CC BY-SA 4.0.
- `GET /2.3/tags?order=desc&sort=popular&pagesize=75`—popular-tag counts.
- `GET /2.3/questions?order=desc&sort=votes&pagesize=100`—top-voted questions (page 1).
- `GET /2.3/tags/{list}/info?site=gis`—exact counts for 29 requested operational tags
  (non-existent tags silently dropped; `snap` resolved to `snapping`).
- **Frames**: `tag_counts` (29×2, counts per operational tag) and the top-voted
  seeded-candidate slice (750 rows × 8 cols, sort=votes desc, pages × 25 for the six
  seeded candidates: **buffer, clip, spatial-join, overlay, zonal-statistics, dissolve**).
- **Execution**: the supplied source describes an interactive analysis; its execution date and counts have not been independently verified. Chart: horizontal bars on a **symlog** scale (a plain log cannot draw zero-baselined bars).
- **Web cross-checks**: two canonical-operation guides (see Sources)—used to sanity-check
  the operation set, not as evidence of effectiveness.
- **Retention**: this page holds aggregates only; the supplied snapshot with an
  unverified retrieval date lives in the [raw notebook page](analyses/gis-se-analysis.md),
  with the fetch recipe and refresh notes.

:::

## Headline findings

1. **CRS is the loudest GIS pain point.** `coordinate-system` = 8 647—more than any
   operational tag—and it dominates the top-100 most-voted questions (EPSG:3857 vs 4326,
   datum vs projection, axis order). The confused-concepts layer is bigger than the
   recipes layer. Good news for trap-task strategy: axis-order/CRS-units traps ask
   well-worn questions, not exotic ones.
2. **The operational core is small.** About a dozen tags cover hands-on asks: buffer,
   clip, merge, spatial-join, overlay, dissolve, zonal-statistics, raster-calculator —
   exactly the proposed catalogue's primitives.
3. **Voting ≠ doing.** The most-upvoted questions are conceptual (CRS, web mapping),
   not operational recipes—"most common question" and "most common task" are different
   distributions. The bank needs both: inherited conceptual traps and constructed
   operational pipelines.
4. **Cartography tags are rare** (`choropleth` 147, `jenks` 9) and standard-class.
   Low SE demand is not low experimental value—the C-family counter-case stands on
   the literature, not on SE volume.
5. **Nobody asks about checkers.** No "validate my CRS/geometry" quality tag exists —
   validation lives inside other questions. This supports predicates-as-oracle by design.
6. **Software context**: qgis 43 077 dominates; the audience is desktop/scripting
   QGIS + ArcGIS—matching the study's toolchain choice.

## Frequency anchor (all-time counts, site=gis)

Bolded rows are the six seeded task-bank candidates.

| Tag | Count | Tag | Count | Tag | Count |
|---|---:|---|---:|---|---:|
| qgis | 43 077 | postgis | 9 580 | pyqgis | 7 931 |
| python | 12 249 | arcpy | 10 662 | raster | 10 203 |
| coordinate-system | 8 647 | gdal | 6 448 | shapefile | 5 698 |
| field-calculator | 2 562 | dem | 2 113 | fields-attributes / attribute-table | 2 003–2 330 |
| distance | 1 620 | **buffer** | **1 533** | **clip** | **1 391** |
| raster-calculator | 1 296 | merge | 1 284 | **spatial-join** | **1 014** |
| interpolation | 932 | geocoding | 870 | topology | 585 |
| routing | 583 | zonal-statistics | **572** | **dissolve** | **547** |
| **overlay** | **512** | snapping | 428 | union | 294 |
| kriging | 277 | nodata | 277 | intersect | 255 |
| simplify | 185 | reverse-geocoding | 151 | choropleth | 147 |

Context (popular non-task tags): qgis-3 4 556 · qgis-plugins 3 175 · arcgis-desktop
21 012 · arcgis-pro 4 126 · arcgis-server 2 749 · arcmap 7 827 · google-earth-engine
5 822 · leaflet 4 195 · openstreetmap 3 330.

![GIS.SE operational tags—demand proxy](assets/gis-se-demand.svg)

*GIS.SE operational tags—demand proxy (supplied snapshot; retrieval date not independently verified). Symlog scale keeps the zero baseline. Top tags by question count; CC BY-SA 4.0.*

## Complexity ranking of the common tasks

Tiers follow the task-suite rubric (tier 1–5 from human tool/step counts). Fam:
P = prepare/IO · A = analysis · C = cartography. **SE anchor** = tag count from the
fetch. **Coverage** = the proposed catalogue (describe/reproject/filter/
buffer/overlay/dissolve/spatial_join/zonal_stats/aggregate/reproject_raster/raster_clip/
reclassify/classify_jenks/render_choropleth).

| # | Task (canonical form) | Fam | Tier | n_tools_h | SE anchor | Coverage | Trap (oracle-relevant) |
|---|---|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| 1 | Identify/set CRS; reproject | P | 1–2 | 1 | 8 647 | `reproject`, `describe_layer` | axis order (4326 vs 2180), degrees vs metres |
| 2 | Select by attribute / filter | P | 1 | 1 | ~2 000–2 330 | `filter` | NULL handling, wrong field type |
| 3 | Field calculation (area, length, units) | P | 1–2 | 1 | 2 562 | **gap**—not exposed | unit mismatch (m² vs ha), CRS-aware area |
| 4 | Format conversion (shp→gpkg, CSV→points) | P | 1 | 1 | 1 474 + 2 701 (geojson) | fixture-time, **not an agent task** | encoding, CRS loss on export |
| 5 | Buffer | P | 2 | 1 | 1 533 | `buffer` | distance unit (deg vs m), ring semantics |
| 6 | Clip / erase | P | 2 | 1 | 1 391 + 82 | `overlay` (intersection/difference) | invalid input geometry → silent GEOS failure |
| 7 | Merge / append layers | P | 2 | 1 | 1 284 | **gap**—not exposed | schema/CRS mismatch across inputs |
| 8 | Dissolve by attribute | P | 2 | 1 | 547 | `dissolve` | premature dissolve (loses counts) |
| 9 | Choropleth (classified) | C | 2–3 | 2–3 | 147 + 9 + 2 390 (symbology) | `classify_jenks`, `render_choropleth` | classification before normalization |
| 10 | Raster clip/mask; window | P/A | 2–3 | 1–2 | 10 203 (raster, broad) | `raster_clip` | NoData propagation, resampling on read |
| 11 | Distance/proximity (within k of) | A | 2–3 | 1–2 | 1 620 | **weak**—buffer+join workaround; no `point_distance` | planar vs geodesic |
| 12 | Spatial join (points-in-polygon, counts) | A | 3 | 1–2 | 1 014 | `spatial_join` | predicate choice (intersects vs within); boundary double-counting |
| 13 | Buffer→clip→dissolve (schools/districts) | P | 3 | 3–5 | 1 533+1 391+547 | full surface | compound error propagation (CRS→buffer→clip) |
| 14 | Overlay (union/intersection/difference) | A | 3 | 1–3 | 512 + 255 + 294 | `overlay` | slivers, topology cracks, attribute merge rules |
| 15 | Zonal statistics (raster stats per polygon) | A | 3 | 1–2 | 572 | `zonal_stats` | NoData policy, partial-cell policy, MAUP |
| 16 | DEM derivatives (slope/aspect/hillshade) | A | 3–4 | 1–3 | 2 113 | **gap**—not exposed | z-factor units, NoData edges |
| 17 | NoData handling in raster pipelines | P/A | 3 | 1–2 | 277 | `zonal_stats(nodata_policy)`, `describe_raster` | silent zero-fill (classic silent corruption) |
| 18 | Raster-calculator map algebra | A | 3–4 | 1–2 | 1 296 | **partial**—`reclassify` only | cell alignment, mask extents, NoData×0 |
| 19 | Labeling/annotation placement | C | 3 | 2–3 | 2 456 (labeling) | **not exposed**—descriptive only | collisions unmeasurable by predicate |
| 20 | Geocoding / reverse geocoding | P | 3 | 1 | 870 + 151 | **out of scope** (needs network) | match ambiguity; inherently soft oracle |
| 21 | Interpolation (IDW; kriging) | A | 4 | 1–2 | 932 + 277 | **not exposed** | model choice, anisotropy |
| 22 | Network analysis (shortest path, isochrones) | A | 4–5 | 2–5 | 583 + 98 | **out of scope v1** | graph defects, direction/turn costs |
| 23 | Watershed / flow accumulation | A | 4–5 | 2–4 | (dem 2 113) | **out of scope v1** | pour-point snapping, NoData sinks |
| 24 | Topology validation & repair | P/A | 4–5 | 2–4 | 585 + 428 | middleware + oracle; **no agent tool by design** | repair masks upstream error |
| 25 | Simplify geometry (Douglas–Peucker) | P/A | 2–3 | 1 | 185 | **gap** | topology break, tolerance units |
| 26 | Concave hull / alpha shapes | A | 4 | 1–2 | exemplary top-100 question (145 votes) | **not exposed** | no unique answer (soft oracle) |
| 27 | Zonation/aggregation sensitivity (MAUP) | A | 5 | 2–5 | no SE tag; literature-anchored | `aggregate`, `zonal_stats` at two zonations | aggregation bias; constructed task |

**Complexity distribution of demand.** Tier 1–2 (CRS fixes, filters, buffer/clip/merge)
accounts for the overwhelming bulk of SE volume; tier 3 (pipelines, spatial join,
zonal stats) is where agents live or die—the A-family sweet spot; tier 4–5 appears
rarely but maps cleanly onto expert tasks and makes good *constructed* tasks.

## Gap analysis vs the proposed catalogue

Missing from the surface that SE says people want:

- `calculate_field` (2 562)—either expose it or GIS-SE-derived tasks involving attribute computation are not agent-expressible.
- `merge` (1 284)—trivial to add, high demand.
- `point_distance` / proximity (1 620)—buffer+join is a workaround, weak for small k.
- `simplify` (185)—low demand; skip.
- Raster: `slope/aspect` and general map algebra—highest-demand raster gap (dem 2 113, raster-calculator 1 296). If the suite gains a second raster task, reconsider a `raster_calc` with a constrained expression grammar (typed enums, not free text).
- Geocoding: deliberately out (offline constraint)—soft oracle anyway.
- Labeling/cartography cosmetics: stays descriptive—no typed tool possible.

:::{important} Catalogue-freeze rule (unchanged)
Whichever subset is exposed must be frozen and hashed before runs. Adding
`calculate_field` / `merge` / `point_distance` **before** freeze is a legitimate
instrument change; after freeze it invalidates the run log.
:::

## Task-bank implications (for the §6.4 freeze)

- **Inherited candidates** (SE-derived, `contamination: inherited`, CC BY-SA 4.0 attribution required): buffer→clip→dissolve pipeline; points-in-polygon join + counts; CRS axis-order reprojection trap (behind 8 647 asks); spatial-join predicate disambiguation.
- **Constructed candidates** (author-made, `contamination: constructed`, CC0): MAUP dual-zonation; NoData-in-zonal-stats; Jenks under normalized vs raw attribute (C-family counter-case); topology/DE-9IM `touches`/`covers` predicate task. Low-SE-volume tasks are *preferable* constructed candidates—no pretraining leakage plausible.
- **Do not inherit verbatim without attribution**—every GIS.SE question carries `content_license: CC BY-SA 4.0`; closed/locked questions may lack the licence field—treat those as unusable for derivation.
- **Jenks (9 questions) ≠ unimportant**—frequency is a demand measure, never a difficulty or representativeness measure.
- **GIS-SE demand data cannot validate the oracle**—it only informs task selection and contamination strata.

## Limitations (read before citing this page)

- Counts are all-time and tool-ecosystem-skewed (ArcGIS|QGIS dominate); no time series, no geography filter, English-only.
- Votes on the top-100 track **conceptual confusion**, not operational need; ~half the headline questions are CRS/datum explainers.
- Tag counts confound "asking" with "doing"; many high-count tags are installation/config/software topics, not tasks.
- Complexity tiers are expert estimates, not measurements; they anchor on the task-suite rubric, pending pilot calibration.
- "Most common GIS tasks ranked by complexity" is not a number GIS.SE publishes; this page is a synthesis, not a dump.
- Licensing: inherited prompts must preserve attribution; constructed traps are the low-risk default.

## Sources (supplied snapshot; retrieval date unverified)

1. `api.stackexchange.com/2.3/tags?order=desc&sort=popular&site=gis&pagesize=75`—popular-tag counts.
2. `api.stackexchange.com/2.3/questions?order=desc&sort=votes&site=gis&pagesize=100`—top-voted questions.
3. `api.stackexchange.com/2.3/tags/buffer;clip;…;extent/info?site=gis`—exact operational counts.
4. Web cross-checks (operation-set sanity only; not evidence of effectiveness): a university spatial-data-processing guide (buffer, dissolve, centroid, spatial selection/joins, overlay); a vendor vector-operations explainer (clip/intersect/difference/union/buffer/dissolve/simplify); an ArcGIS geoprocessing overview (buffer, clip, intersect, union, dissolve, merge, erase).
5. All GIS Stack Exchange content: **CC BY-SA 4.0**—attribution carried in task `provenance.license` fields and in the repository's attribution file at freeze.

# === reproducibility.md ===

---
title: Reproducibility
short_title: Reproducibility
description: >-
  The run contract: environment, pins, freeze order, and what never enters the
  repository.
---

(reproducibility)=

## Environment

```bash
pixi install --locked        # environment from the committed pixi.lock
pixi run tools ls            # task graph sanity
pixi run tools check         # alint + ruff + pytest + rumdl (offline gate)
pixi run tools run prose     # Vale prose gate (downloads presets; network required)
```

- **pixi only** for Python environments. No `uv`, `pip`, `requirements.txt`, `venv`.
- Python 3.12–3.13. Bun is pinned for agent-skill/Backlog.md CLIs only.
- The `docs` feature uses its own solve group. At present, the `experiment` feature is
  included in `default` alongside tooling; split it into a dedicated solve group before
  measurement runs if GIS dependency growth or incompatibilities affect the automation environment.
- This documentation site builds with the pinned MyST CLI:

```bash
pixi install --locked --environment docs
pixi run --environment docs -- npm exec --yes --package=mystmd@1.13.0 -- myst build --html --strict --ci
```

- The `docs/analyses/` page is a raw marimo notebook rendered at build time through
  the `jupyter-book-marimo` executable plugin (registered in `docs/myst.yml`). It uses
  an embedded public-source snapshot, not a committed API cache; the snapshot's retrieval
  date and values are not independently verified, so validate them before relying on the analysis.

## Pins and determinism

| Item | Contract |
|---|---|
| Model | OpenCode-hosted BigPickle; pin what the provider exposes (`model_id`, `run_date`, driver hash, temperature); accept the rest as bounded variance (r = 4) |
| Engine | QGIS LTR, dedicated profile; PROJ/GDAL versions pinned and recorded |
| Python libs | `geopandas`, `shapely`, `pyproj`, `rasterio`, `pyogrio` (locked via pixi) |
| Oracle | 3× determinism gate on fixed artefacts—blocking, pre-freeze |
| Randomisation | stratum-interleaved order; seed table frozen with `v1.0-prereg` |
| Runs | N ≥ 80 tasks × r = 4 (scaled); 200-run pilot ceiling as budgeted |

## What is never in this repository

- Private datasets, fixtures with personal data, unpublished results, run archives,
  experiment caches, or task-suite artefacts outside the registered freeze process.
  The documented Stack Exchange aggregates are public-source research context with
  CC BY-SA 4.0 attribution, not experiment run data.
- The thesis, its literature review, and its data analyses—they live in the
  surrounding workspace, not here.
- Secrets and API tokens—the model provider is called with environment variables,
  never committed config.

`docs/_build/` is gitignored; the built site deploys from CI artifacts, never from a local build.

## Freeze and re-verification

- Tag `v1.0-prereg` = specification amendment state + task checksums + seed table.
- Any post-freeze change to tolerances, hypotheses or stop-rules **invalidates the run
  log** and must ship as a new preregistration revision, never a silent edit.
- Changes to this site are gated in CI (Markdown, prose, strict MyST build) on every
  pull request.

## This site's own reproducibility

Pages are plain MyST Markdown; `docs/bibliography.bib` is a dated snapshot of the source
corpus; `robots.txt`, `sitemap.xml`, `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt` are static files
served at the site root exactly as committed. The raw analyses execute at build
time; the outputs are baked into static HTML and hydrate in the browser.
